notes_for_editor: Thin record. For Mount Nehasane itself the only source read is the FFLA county line (Platform Tower Gone, Hamilton County, coordinates 43.98871, -74.81432, which match the brief); the county is now in the quoted evidence. No source read gives a build date, builder, staffing or removal date for the Mount Nehasane platform, so none is stated. The story covers the Webb family's Mount Electra tower only as park context and says it is a different lookout. Conflict on the Electra fate: NYSFFLA says it was dismantled in 1989 and left at the site; Adirondack Life says it was pushed over, with no date. The FFLA Herkimer County list also has an 'Electra, Mount' line marked Tower Gone (43.98258, -74.84528); the story does not cite it. NYSFFLA also says its construction date cannot be verified. Two Facebook posts (FFLA NY chapter, and History and Legends of the Adirondacks) were seen only as search snippets and were not readable; they claim a Nehasane tower was still present in 1919 and that Webb moved a steel tower to Rock Lake Mountain. NYSFFLA's Moose River entry says a steel tower bought in 1919 went to a site near Thendara. Those claims were not quoted and are unresolved. Access and today's condition are unset: no source describes the Mount Nehasane site now. Brief check: kind platform and status gone match FFLA; no corrections proposed.
